brief: Micron reports its August quarter after the close, with sentiment described as less euphoric than ahead of the June print, when Micron beat Q2 revenue ($41.5BN vs $35.7BN expected) and margin (84.9% vs 81.9%) estimates and guided August to $49-51BN, prompting SK Hynix and Kioxia to rally in sympathy. Goldman expects another beat and a November guide above consensus ($57.7BN vs $56.7BN), with Jim Schneider above Street estimates (median sellside: $51.49bn revenue, 86.2% margin, $31.83 EPS) across the board. Positioning feels relatively balanced, but investors expect the shift toward Strategic Customer Agreements, long-term floor-priced contracts, to cap beat magnitude below Micron's typical 10-30% EPS beats over the last six quarters, trading beat size for earnings durability. The swing factors are SCA mix, capital-return size and timing once CHIPS Act restrictions lift in December (JPMorgan expects cumulative FCF near $200BN through 2027), and HBM share. Asia markets are watching closely: Samsung and SK Hynix buybacks are nearly finished, raising liquidity-void concerns, while regional memory stocks remain well below their peaks.
